info.title: Oxide API
info.summary: Text, markdown and structured PDF extraction, with OCR.
info.description:
One HTTP API that extracts `text` and `markdown` from **PDF**, **Office** (DOCX, XLSX, PPTX,
DOC, XLS, PPT), **OpenDocument** (ODT, ODS, ODP) and **image** files (PNG, JPEG, TIFF, WebP,
GIF, BMP, JPEG 2000, PNM, TGA). The file type is detected from the content, so one route
serves every format.

PDF pages are classified one by one: pages with a usable text layer are extracted natively,
and scanned or legacy-font pages go through OCR (English, Hindi, Arabic, Tamil) in the same request.
Images go straight to OCR, one page per TIFF page; EXIF orientation is honoured. HEIC, AVIF
and JPEG XL are recognized but not supported.

**Input.** Send the document as multipart (`file=<binary>`), as JSON
(`{"file_base64": "..."}`), or as the raw request body. Parameters are top-level multipart
parts, JSON keys, or query parameters; body parameters override query parameters. Parameters
that don't apply to the detected document kind are ignored and listed in `ignored_params`.

**Output.** JSON by default. `Accept: text/plain` (text endpoint) or `Accept: text/markdown`
(markdown endpoint) returns the raw text, with metadata in `X-Oxide-*` headers.

**OCR engines.** Select `ocr_engine=paddle|indra` (default Paddle). Indra runs
locally as a CLI with one core and bounded batches. Math is on by default and
can be disabled with `OXIDE_API_INDRA_MATH=false`. `include_debug=true` returns
ordered flow steps and textual input/output in JSON, bounded by the configured
debug byte budget. No binary uploads or credentials are returned in debug.

**Structured PDF.** `/v1/extract/document` returns page text and ordered, positioned blocks
for digital, scanned and mixed PDFs. Native font details and OCR recognizer confidence are
retained; unavailable confidence is null. This is input for downstream LLM schema mapping;
the service does not call an LLM or accept a target JSON schema.

**Fields.** `/v1/extract/fields` reads the document exactly as the text endpoint does, then
runs a list of named regular-expression fields over that one text and returns each value (or
`null`). Its `fields` (and `text`) are taken whole, the one exception to "never nested".

**Limits.** 32 MiB request body (for JSON this counts the base64 text). 8 requests are
processed at once per container; others wait up to 1 s for a slot, then get `429`.
Native extraction has a 30 s deadline, requests that OCR any page 120 s, both measured from
admission. A PDF or image that runs out of time returns the pages done so far with
`incomplete: true`. Images are limited to 64 megapixels per page.

Errors use RFC 9457 `application/problem+json`.

post.description:
Office and OpenDocument: the document's plain text. PDF: per-page native text, with OCR
for pages that need it. Images: OCR text per page. Pages are joined with a blank line.

post.summary: Extract structured PDF content for downstream schema mapping
post.description:
PDF only; digital, scanned and mixed pages share the text endpoint's classification,
language resolution, OCR workers, admission, limits and error handling. Always JSON,
including with Accept: text/plain. No LLM calls or schema mapping are performed.

Native pages use PDF-Oxide positioned spans in its Structure reading order (geometric
column order with tagged table ordering where supported). OCR pages are rendered once
and reuse the existing recognizers, preserving detected text regions and recognition
confidence. Mixed pages retain native text, discard duplicate OCR regions using the
text endpoint's line comparison, and sort the combined blocks geometrically.
Reading order and heading roles are best effort; this is not table-cell reconstruction.

All boxes use points in the visible page after CropBox clipping and Rotate, with origin
at top-left, x right and y down. `page.text` is the blocks joined with newlines.
`char_count` sums page text Unicode scalar counts. The text budget counts that text
once, including separators, and can shorten the final block (its box still bounds the
original region). Pages omitted by a deadline or budget are absent from pages_extracted.
`incomplete` means deadline; `truncated` means budget. Empty pages remain present.

Confidence is null for native text (including an existing scanner OCR layer) and when
unavailable; it is never a general extraction quality score. For OCR it is the engine
recognition score in [0,1], character-weighted when the existing recognizer splits a
region into words. No synthetic page or document confidence is calculated.

200.description: Structured pages; check incomplete, truncated and OCR availability before mapping.

post.description:
Office and OpenDocument: markdown rendering of the document structure (headings, lists,
tables). PDF: per-page markdown with heading detection; OCR'd pages and images contribute
their lines and paragraphs.

Reads the document to its final text exactly as `/v1/extract/text` does (native text, OCR
where pages need it, Arabic presentation forms normalized, `clean` when asked), then runs
every field in `fields` over that one text: no field causes OCR of its own. Send `text`
instead of a document to run the fields over text you already have (from an earlier
extraction, say) without reading anything again.

Each field's patterns are tried in order; the first **valid** match wins. A match is valid
when its capture group took part, is not blank, reads as the field's `type`, and fits
`max_length`; an invalid match is skipped, never cut down. With `multiple`, every valid
match of every pattern is kept in that order, each distinct value once (at most 1000).
Values are the text as read, trimmed, or for a typed field in its type's form (a date
`YYYY-MM-DD`, an amount a plain decimal): nothing is corrected. `matched` holds what each
value was read from, as printed, for marking it in the text.

Every requested field is in the response: its value, an array (`multiple`), or `null` when
nothing matched — never left out, unlike the optional keys of the other responses.
Required fields that matched nothing are also listed in `missing_required`; the request
still succeeds.

Patterns are Rust `regex` syntax, matched in time linear in the text: inline flags such as
`(?i)` (case), `(?m)` (`^`/`$` per line) and `(?s)` (`.` crosses lines) work; look-around
and backreferences do not and are refused with the engine's reason. `\d`, `\w` and
`(?i)` are Unicode-aware, so `\d` also matches Arabic-Indic and Devanagari digits. A
value on the line after its label is reached with `\s+` (`Label\s+([^\n]+)`).

Specs are checked before the document is read, so a bad pattern costs a `400` and no OCR.
A request holds at most 50 fields and 100 patterns of at most 1000 characters each.
Counted repetitions of broad classes compile large (`\w{1,200}` is ~10 MiB, the most one
pattern may take; `[A-Za-z0-9]{1,200}` a fraction of that); the larger patterns of one
request share a 40 MiB budget.

Matching has a deadline of its own, the 30 s native deadline started afresh once the text
is read, because OCR may have used the request's. So a request that OCRs can run past the
120 s OCR deadline by that much; matching is linear in the text and normally takes
milliseconds.

Always JSON: `Accept` is not negotiated.

Office and OpenDocument: format, core metadata, and structure (sheet names and
dimensions, slide count, section count). PDF: metadata, page count, encryption flag and
per-page geometry. Images: page count and pixel dimensions, read from the headers only.

get.description: Fails (503) only when the watchdog sees a job running longer than 10x its deadline.
Ready once startup (including OCR model loading and golden smoke tests) is done; 503 while starting or draining.

get.summary: Build, engine versions, limits and OCR status
Interactive API reference (Scalar, loaded from a CDN)

format.name: format
format.description:
Format hint, used only when the content itself is inconclusive (the content sniff always
wins). Aliases are accepted too: template and macro-enabled extensions (`dotx`, `xlsm`,
`ott`, ...), `jpg`, `tif`, `pbm`/`pgm`/`ppm`, `j2k`. TGA has no signature, so a TGA needs
this hint or a `.tga` filename.

pages.name: pages
pages.description: PDF and images (TIFF pages). 1-based pages and ranges, e.g. `1-3,5`.

ocr.name: ocr
ocr.description:
PDF and images. PDF: `auto` OCRs pages classified as scanned, hybrid or set in a legacy
Hindi font; `force` OCRs every requested page; `off` skips classification. Images are
always OCR'd unless `off`.

ocr_engine.name: ocr_engine
ocr_engine.description:
PDF and images. Select PaddleOCR or the Indra CLI. Paddle is the default.
The selected engine obeys ocr=auto|force|off and pages. Indra uses automatic
script selection; lang is ignored and listed in ignored_params. Indra math
is enabled by default; OXIDE_API_INDRA_MATH=false disables it server-wide.
A needed but unavailable Indra installation returns 503 ocr-unavailable.

include_debug.name: include_debug
include_debug.description:
Return debug.steps with ordered parser/routing/OCR input and output, status
and elapsed_ms. Indra includes its CLI JSON and settings. Upload bytes,
filenames, credentials, local paths and subprocess stderr are excluded.
Payloads share OXIDE_API_MAX_DEBUG_BYTES (default 1048576); omitted data
carries truncated=true, original_bytes and a preview. debug.truncated marks
any omission. This option forces JSON even when Accept requests raw text.
Off by default. Diagnostics contain document text and are never logged.

lang.name: lang
lang.description:
PDF and images. PaddleOCR language (ignored by Indra). `auto` resolves once per document: legacy Hindi font →
`hi`; else the native text's script; else a confidence probe on the first OCR page; else
`en`.

detect_headings.name: detect_headings
detect_headings.description: PDF markdown only. Detect headings from font size and weight.

clean.name: clean
clean.description:
Any document. When `true`, extra whitespace is collapsed: runs of spaces and tabs
become a single space, trailing whitespace on each line is removed, 3+ newlines
become a single blank line, and leading/trailing blank lines are trimmed.
Markdown code-block indentation is collapsed to a single space.

include_text.name: include_text
include_text.description:
`/v1/extract/fields` only. Also return the text the fields ran over, so a caller that
indexes the text and wants fields gets both from one read of the document.

filename.name: filename
filename.description: Original filename; its extension is the last-resort format hint (after the content and `format`).

file_base64.description: Base64 (standard or URL-safe; a `data:` URI prefix is accepted).

additionalProperties.description: Parameters are top-level scalars, never nested.

application/octet-stream.description: Any other content type is treated as the raw document.

FieldsInput.description:
A document, as for the other endpoints, or `text` — not both — plus `fields`. In a JSON
body `fields` is the array itself; as a multipart part or query parameter it is that array
as a JSON string. A raw body can carry it only in the query string (4096 characters), so
send JSON or multipart for anything longer.

file_base64.description: The document, base64 (standard or URL-safe; a `data:` URI prefix is accepted).

text.description: Text to run the fields over instead of a document.

fields.description: The field specs as a JSON array.

text.description: Text to run the fields over instead of `file`.

application/octet-stream.description: The raw document, with `fields` in the query string.

X-Engine.description:
Engine and version: `pdf_oxide/0.3.78` (PDFs, and image OCR), `office_oxide/0.1.13`
(DOCX/XLSX/PPTX/DOC/XLS/PPT) or `oxide-api/0.3.1` (OpenDocument, image info).

Server-Timing.description: `queue`, `parse`, `extract` and (when OCR ran) `ocr` durations in ms.

BadRequest.description: Malformed input or an invalid parameter (the problem names the accepted values).

UploadTimeout.description: The request body took longer than 30 s to arrive.

TooLarge.description: The request body is over the 32 MiB limit.

Unprocessable.description:
Unsupported, corrupt or encrypted document (`encrypted-document`, `corrupt-document`,
`unsupported-format`, `too-many-pages`, `image-too-large`), a processing timeout
(`processing-timeout`), or every page's OCR failing with `ocr=force` or on an image
(`ocr-failed`).

Busy.description: No processing slot became free within 1 s. Honour `Retry-After`.

Draining.description: The instance is shutting down, or a requested Indra CLI/model installation is unavailable (ocr-unavailable).

input.description: Stage settings and input metadata or text; bounded when oversized.

output.description: Full textual stage results within the shared debug budget.

char_count.description: Sum of Unicode scalar values in page text.

width.description: Visible rotated page width in points.

height.description: Visible rotated page height in points.

text.description: Ordered block text joined with newlines.

truncated.description: This page lost text to the document budget.

id.description: Page-scoped citation ID, e.g. p1-b0; deterministic for the same extraction, not a persistent document ID.

reading_order.description: Zero-based position in this page's blocks array.

bbox.description: Axis-aligned region in displayed page points; null when source geometry is unavailable.

confidence.description: OCR recognition confidence only; null for native text or unavailable scores. Word-split regions use character-weighted engine scores.

size.description: Native font size in PDF points.

truncated.description: The 4 Mi-character output budget ran out.

incomplete.description: The deadline passed; request the missing pages with `pages=`.

failed_pages.description: Pages whose native text could not be extracted (omitted when empty).

ignored_params.description: Parameters that don't apply to this document (omitted when empty).

engine.description: Selected OCR backend; pages lists actual OCR use.

status.description:
`native`: no page needed OCR. `ocr`: every page came from OCR. `hybrid`: a mix, or
native text plus OCR lines. `unavailable`: OCR was needed but isn't available here
(models not loaded, or the language isn't available). `off`: `ocr=off`.

pages.description: Pages whose output includes OCR text.

pages_needing_ocr.description: Pages that need OCR but didn't get it (OCR unavailable for them).

failed_pages.description: Pages whose OCR failed; they carry native text, or none when the page's OCR layer was junk.

reasons.description: Why each page was routed to OCR (omitted when none was).

ImageExtraction.description: Same shape as a PDF extraction; every page comes from OCR.

FieldSpec.description: One named value to read out of the text. Unknown keys are refused.

name.description: The key of the value in `fields`; unique within the request.

patterns.description: Regular expressions (Rust `regex` syntax), tried in order.

capture_group.description:
The group that is the value: a number (`0` is the whole match) or a group name
(`(?<name>...)`). It must exist in every pattern. Omitted: group 1 for a pattern that
has one, the whole match for a pattern that has none.

required.description: A required field that matches nothing is listed in `missing_required`.

type.description:
What the value must be. A match that does not read as its type is not a valid match:
the next one is tried. The value is written in one form whatever the print, and
nothing is corrected (an `O` read for a `0` fails the check):

- `date`: `YYYY-MM-DD`. Numeric (`14/10/2026`, `14.10.26`, `2026-10-14`) or with an
  English month name (`14 Oct 2026`, `14th October, 2026`, `Oct 14, 2026`, `Wed, 14 Oct 2026`);
  a day the month does not have is not a date. A two-digit year below 70 is 20xx, else 19xx.
- `amount`: a plain decimal, `-` when negative (`-`, a trailing `-`, or brackets).
  A sign and currency around the number are allowed (`Rs.`, `₹`, `USD`, `US$`, `1,250/-`,
  `1 250,00 €`); digits grouped in threes or Indian style (`1,25,000`), one separator kind.
  Decimal digits are kept as printed, never rounded: `₹ 1,25,000.50` → `125000.50`.
- `gstin`: 15 characters, upper-case, spaces and hyphens removed; the check character must match.
- `pan`: `AAAAA9999A`, upper-case; the shape only.
- `iban`: upper-case without spaces; the ISO 13616 mod-97 check must pass.

A capture over 64 characters is never a typed value.

format.description:
`date`: how an all-numeric date is read, `dmy` (default), `mdy` or `ymd`; four digits
first is always year-month-day. `amount`: the decimal mark, `point` (default,
`1,250.00`) or `comma` (`1.250,00`). Refused for other types.

normalization.description:
`trim` removes leading and trailing whitespace; `none` keeps the capture as matched.
A `text` field's only: a typed value is always written in its type's form.

max_length.description: A longer value is not a valid match; the next one is tried. Characters of the value as returned.

multiple.description: Return every distinct valid match, in order, as an array.

selection.description: Which valid match is the value. Only `first` today.

FieldsExtraction.description:
`kind` is the document's, or `text` when `text` was sent; a PDF or image adds the same
page and OCR details as its text extraction.

format.description: As in the text extraction; absent for `text`.

fields.description: Every requested field, in request order.

matched.description:
What each value was read from, as printed, keyed like `fields`: the text to look for
when marking a value, since a typed value (`2026-10-14`) is not in the text and its
print (`14 Oct 2026`) is. A `multiple` field lists every distinct print of the values
kept; `null` where nothing matched.

missing_required.description: Required fields that matched nothing, in request order.

char_count.description: Unicode scalar values in the text the fields ran over.

truncated.description: The 4 Mi-character budget ran out: later text was never searched.

incomplete.description: The deadline passed before every page was read; values on the missing pages were not seen.

text.description: The text the fields ran over (`include_text` only).

parameter.description: The offending parameter (400 only); for a field spec, its place, e.g. `fields[1].patterns[0]`.
